abs.title: How f64::abs works
abs.description: The distance from zero: removes the minus sign.

slides.caption: abs gives the size of the number without its sign.
Comparing floats: (a - b).abs() < 1e-9 instead of a == b.

max.title: How f64::max works
max.description: The larger of two floats; ignores NaN.

slides.caption: Floats are not Ord (because of NaN), so they have their own max.
If one side is NaN, the other number is returned.
The largest float in a list: v.iter().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max).

clamp.title: How f64::clamp works
clamp.description: Keeps a float inside a range.

slides.caption: clamp returns the number if it is inside the range, otherwise the nearest end.
Handy for percentages, colours and volumes. clamp panics if min > max.

min.title: How f64::min works
min.description: The smaller of two floats; ignores NaN.

slides.caption: f64::min compares two floats; if one is NaN, the other one wins.
The smallest of a list: v.iter().copied().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min).

signum.title: How f64::signum works
signum.description: 1.0 for positive numbers, -1.0 for negative ones.

slides.caption: signum keeps only the sign of the number.
Useful for directions: velocity.signum() is +1 or -1.

is_nan.title: How f64::is_nan works
is_nan.description: true for NaN, the "not a number" value.

note.text: NaN is not even equal to itself

slides.caption: 0.0 / 0.0 has no answer, so it gives NaN. 1.0 / 0.0 gives infinity, which is not NaN.
x == f64::NAN is always false, so you must use is_nan().

total_cmp.title: How f64::total_cmp works
total_cmp.description: A full ordering of floats, so they can be sorted.

slides.caption: Vec<f64> has no sort() because of NaN. total_cmp defines an order for every float.
NaN values end up at the edges instead of breaking the sort.

to_radians.title: How f64::to_radians works
to_radians.description: Converts degrees to radians, which sin and cos expect.

slides.caption: Trigonometry in Rust works in radians: a full turn is 2π, not 360.
to_degrees goes back. x.to_radians().sin() is the sine of x degrees.

checked_add.title: How checked_add works
checked_add.description: Adds two integers; None instead of overflowing.

slides.caption: checked_add returns Some(sum) when the result fits in the type, and None when it does not.
Use it when overflow is a real possibility, e.g. sizes read from a file.

checked_sub.title: How checked_sub works
checked_sub.description: Subtracts; None if the result would not fit.

slides.caption: For unsigned types, going below zero is an overflow too.
3 - 5 would be -2, which a u32 cannot hold: None.
A common case: index.checked_sub(1) when the index might be 0.
Products grow fast; checked_mul catches the moment they stop fitting.
Ten billion does not fit in an i32: None.
Chain with ?: a.checked_mul(b)?.checked_add(c) inside a function returning Option.

checked_div.title: How checked_div works
checked_div.description: Divides; None when dividing by zero (or on overflow).

slides.caption: Plain 7 / 0 panics. checked_div turns that into None.
For signed types, i32::MIN / -1 also overflows and gives None.

checked_rem.title: How checked_rem works
checked_rem.description: The remainder; None when dividing by zero.

slides.caption: For negative numbers use rem_euclid if you want a result that is never negative.

checked_pow.title: How checked_pow works
checked_pow.description: Raises to a power; None on overflow.

slides.caption: checked_pow multiplies step by step and stops if a step overflows.
2^40 is about a trillion: too big for i32.
The exponent is always a u32.

checked_neg.title: How checked_neg works
checked_neg.description: Negates; None when the negative does not fit.

slides.caption: Signed types have one more negative number than positive ones, so the smallest cannot be negated.
+128 does not fit in an i8: None.
For unsigned types, only 0 can be negated.

wrapping_add.title: How wrapping_add works
wrapping_add.description: Adds and wraps around past the maximum, like a car odometer.

slides.caption: wrapping_add keeps only the bits that fit: for u8, the result is (a + b) mod 256.
Used on purpose in hashes, checksums and random number generators.

wrapping_sub.title: How wrapping_sub works
wrapping_sub.description: Subtracts and wraps around below the minimum.

slides.caption: Below 0, a u8 wraps to the top: 0 - 1 is 255.

wrapping_mul.title: How wrapping_mul works
wrapping_mul.description: Multiplies and keeps only the low bits that fit.

slides.caption: The true product is computed, then reduced modulo 2^bits.
Typical in hash functions: h = h.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(c).

wrapping_neg.title: How wrapping_neg works
wrapping_neg.description: Negates, wrapping around: for unsigned types this gives 2^bits - x.

slides.caption: Negating 1 in a u8 wraps to 255; i8::MIN stays i8::MIN.
+128 does not fit in an i8, so it wraps back to -128.
x & x.wrapping_neg() isolates the lowest set bit.

saturating_add.title: How saturating_add works
saturating_add.description: Adds, but stops at the maximum instead of overflowing.

slides.caption: Like a volume knob: it goes up to the maximum and stays there.
300 would overflow: the result sticks at 255.
150 fits, so it is the normal sum.
Good for colours, health points and counters that must not wrap.

saturating_sub.title: How saturating_sub works
saturating_sub.description: Subtracts, but stops at the minimum (0 for unsigned).

slides.caption: saturating_sub is the safe way to subtract unsigned numbers.
3 - 5 would go below 0: the result is 0.

saturating_mul.title: How saturating_mul works
saturating_mul.description: Multiplies, clamping at the minimum or maximum.

slides.caption: The result is the true product, or the closest value the type can hold.
The sign of the true answer decides which end it sticks to.

saturating_pow.title: How saturating_pow works
saturating_pow.description: Raises to a power, clamping at the limits.

slides.caption: saturating_pow never overflows: too large becomes the maximum.
checked_pow tells you it overflowed; saturating_pow just caps the value.

overflowing_add.title: How overflowing_add works
overflowing_add.description: Adds and wraps, and also tells you whether it overflowed.

slides.caption: overflowing_add returns a pair: the wrapped result and a flag.
260 wraps to 4, and the flag is true.
Building block for big-number arithmetic: the flag is the carry.

overflowing_sub.title: How overflowing_sub works
overflowing_sub.description: Subtracts and wraps, plus a flag that says it overflowed.

slides.caption: The result wraps like wrapping_sub; the bool reports it.
The bool is called the borrow when subtracting multi-word numbers.

overflowing_mul.title: How overflowing_mul works
overflowing_mul.description: Multiplies and wraps, plus an overflow flag.

slides.caption: 272 does not fit in a u8; 272 mod 256 is 16.
Use checked_mul when you only need to know if it fits.

pow.title: How pow works
pow.description: Raises an integer to a power: x multiplied by itself n times.

slides.caption: Overflow panics in debug builds; use checked_pow or saturating_pow when the result may be large. For floats use powi or powf.

rem_euclid.title: How rem_euclid works
rem_euclid.description: A remainder that is never negative.

note.text: % keeps the sign of the left side

slides.caption: For negative numbers, % gives a negative remainder; rem_euclid always lands in 0..3.
Perfect for wrapping indexes: (i - 1).rem_euclid(len) never goes negative.

div_euclid.title: How div_euclid works
div_euclid.description: Division that rounds so the remainder is never negative.

slides.caption: / rounds toward zero. div_euclid rounds down for positive divisors, matching rem_euclid.
Useful for grid cells: which tile is at coordinate -7 if tiles are 3 wide? Tile -3.

abs_diff.title: How abs_diff works
abs_diff.description: The distance between two numbers, as an unsigned value.

slides.caption: abs_diff never underflows, even for unsigned types where 3 - 10 would panic.
For signed types it returns the unsigned type: (-5i32).abs_diff(5) is 10u32.

isqrt.title: How isqrt works
isqrt.description: The integer square root: the largest n with n × n ≤ x.

slides.caption: isqrt works on integers directly, without going through floats.
Signed types panic on negative numbers; checked_isqrt returns None instead.

ilog2.title: How ilog2 works
ilog2.description: How many times you can halve a number before it drops below 2: floor(log₂ x).

note.text: the index of the highest 1 bit

slides.caption: It panics for 0; checked_ilog2 returns None. ilog2 + 1 is the number of bits needed.

ilog10.title: How ilog10 works
ilog10.description: floor(log₁₀ x): one less than the number of decimal digits.

slides.caption: ilog10 counts how many times you can divide by 10 and stay at least 1.

ilog.title: How ilog works
ilog.description: floor(log of x in any base).

slides.caption: ilog(b) finds the largest k with b^k ≤ x.
ilog2 and ilog10 are faster versions for bases 2 and 10.
Useful with bit flags: how many options are switched on.

count_zeros.title: How count_zeros works
count_zeros.description: How many bits are 0, counting the full width of the type.

slides.caption: count_ones + count_zeros is always the bit width (8 here).

leading_zeros.title: How leading_zeros works
leading_zeros.description: How many 0 bits come before the first 1.

slides.caption: Count from the left (the most significant bit) until the first 1.
Bit width minus leading_zeros is the number of bits the value really needs.

trailing_zeros.title: How trailing_zeros works
trailing_zeros.description: How many 0 bits come after the last 1: how often 2 divides the number.

slides.caption: Count from the right until the first 1.
Bit sets use it to find the lowest member quickly.

leading_ones.title: How leading_ones works
leading_ones.description: How many 1 bits come before the first 0.

slides.caption: leading_ones counts the run of 1s at the top.
In UTF-8, leading_ones of the first byte tells how many bytes the character uses.

trailing_ones.title: How trailing_ones works
trailing_ones.description: How many 1 bits there are at the right end.

slides.caption: trailing_ones counts the run of 1s at the bottom.
x.trailing_ones() is the index of the lowest 0 bit.

rotate_left.title: How rotate_left works
rotate_left.description: Shifts bits left; bits that fall off the top come back at the bottom.

slides.caption: The top 1 leaves on the left...
rotate_right goes the other way. Common in hash functions and ciphers.

rotate_right.title: How rotate_right works
rotate_right.description: Shifts bits right; bits that fall off the bottom come back at the top.

slides.caption: The lowest bit wraps around to the highest position.

reverse_bits.title: How reverse_bits works
reverse_bits.description: Mirrors the bits: the first becomes the last.

slides.caption: Every bit moves to the mirrored position.
Used in FFT and some CRC algorithms.

swap_bytes.title: How swap_bytes works
swap_bytes.description: Reverses the order of the bytes.

slides.caption: swap_bytes converts between big-endian and little-endian layouts.
Usually you want to_be_bytes / from_le_bytes instead, which say what they mean.

to_be_bytes.title: How to_be_bytes works
to_be_bytes.description: The bytes of the number, most significant first (big-endian).

slides.caption: Big-endian puts the "big end" first, the way we write numbers.
Network protocols and many file formats use big-endian.

to_le_bytes.title: How to_le_bytes works
to_le_bytes.description: The bytes of the number, least significant first (little-endian).

slides.caption: Little-endian puts the lowest byte first.
Most CPUs store numbers this way; formats like PNG use big-endian.

from_be_bytes.title: How from_be_bytes works
from_be_bytes.description: Builds a number from bytes, most significant first.

slides.caption: The first byte is the high part: 1 × 256 + 0.
The array length must match the type: 2 bytes for u16, 4 for u32.

from_le_bytes.title: How from_le_bytes works
from_le_bytes.description: Builds a number from bytes, least significant first.

slides.caption: The first byte is the low part: 1 + 0 × 256.
The same two bytes mean 256 in big-endian: always know which order a format uses.

int-abs.title: How abs works
int-abs.description: The absolute value: the number without its sign.

slides.caption: abs turns negative numbers positive and leaves positive ones alone.
i32::MIN.abs() overflows; unsigned_abs() or checked_abs() avoid that. Write (-7i32).abs(): -7i32.abs() means -(7.abs()).
signum reduces a number to its direction.
For comparisons, a.cmp(&b) gives an Ordering, which is usually clearer.
is_negative is the same as x < 0.
is_positive is the counterpart; 0 is neither.
is_positive is the same as x > 0.
Only signed integer types have it.

unsigned_abs.title: How unsigned_abs works
unsigned_abs.description: The absolute value as the unsigned type, so it can never overflow.

slides.caption: abs() of i8::MIN would be 128, which an i8 cannot hold. A u8 can.
Ideal when you need the size of a value no matter its sign.

checked_abs.title: How checked_abs works
checked_abs.description: abs, but None for the one value that has no positive twin.

slides.caption: For every value except MIN, the absolute value fits.
MIN has no positive counterpart: None.
wrapping_abs returns MIN unchanged; saturating_abs returns MAX.

checked_add_unsigned.title: How checked_add_unsigned works
checked_add_unsigned.description: Adds an unsigned amount to a signed number; None on overflow.

slides.caption: No cast needed: the unsigned amount is added directly.
The unsigned twin is checked_add_signed, for adding a possibly negative offset to a usize.
A power of two has exactly one bit set.
0 is not a power of two. Only unsigned types have this method.

next_power_of_two.title: How next_power_of_two works
next_power_of_two.description: The smallest power of two that is at least the number.

slides.caption: Numbers that already are powers of two stay the same.
Buffers and hash tables often size themselves this way. checked_next_power_of_two returns None on overflow.

note.text: how many boxes of 3 for 10 items?

slides.caption: Normal / rounds down; div_ceil rounds any remainder up.

next_multiple_of.title: How next_multiple_of works
next_multiple_of.description: Rounds up to the next multiple of a number.

slides.caption: The smallest multiple of 8 that is at least the number.
Typical for aligning sizes and offsets in memory or in files.

is_multiple_of.title: How is_multiple_of works
is_multiple_of.description: true if the number divides evenly.

slides.caption: is_multiple_of reads better than % and does not panic for 0.
12 is not a multiple of 5: false.
0 is a multiple of everything, even 0.
x % 0 would panic; is_multiple_of(0) is only true for x == 0.

checked_add_signed.title: How checked_add_signed works
checked_add_signed.description: Adds a possibly negative offset to an unsigned number; None if it leaves the range.

slides.caption: Great for moving an index by -1 or +1 without casts.
saturating_add_signed and wrapping_add_signed are the other flavours.

int.title: How parse works for integers
int.description: Turns text such as "42" into an integer, or an error if it is not a valid number.

slides.caption: The type you ask for decides what counts as valid: its sign and its range.
"-7": a minus sign is fine for signed types.
300 is too big for a u8: PosOverflow.
Spaces are not allowed: call trim() first. Use ? or match to handle the Err.

float.title: How parse works for floats
float.description: Turns text such as "2.5" or "1e3" into an f64 or f32.

slides.caption: Float parsing accepts decimals, exponents and the words inf and NaN.
A comma is not a decimal point: Err.
Rust always uses a dot, whatever the computer's language settings are.

is_ascii_digit.title: How u8::is_ascii_digit works
is_ascii_digit.description: true for the bytes b'0' to b'9'.

slides.caption: b'7' is the byte 55, the code of the character 7. The number 7 is a control code, not a digit.
Turn a digit byte into its value with b - b'0'.
Works on raw bytes, e.g. while scanning s.as_bytes().
Identifiers usually also allow _: c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'_'.

is_ascii_whitespace.title: How u8::is_ascii_whitespace works
is_ascii_whitespace.description: true for space, tab, newline, carriage return and form feed.

slides.caption: Vertical tab (\x0B) is not included, unlike some other languages.
Digits and symbols are neither upper nor lower case.

is_ascii_punctuation.title: How u8::is_ascii_punctuation works
is_ascii_punctuation.description: true for printable symbols such as ! , . ? - _

slides.caption: Every printable ASCII character that is not a letter, a digit or a space.
Hex uses 16 digits: 0–9 and a–f (either case).
Check colours like "#ff8800" byte by byte.

to_ascii_uppercase.title: How u8::to_ascii_uppercase works
to_ascii_uppercase.description: The capital version of a small ASCII letter; other bytes stay the same.

slides.caption: Only a–z change; they move 32 places down the ASCII table.
Capitals and digits stay as they are.
to_ascii_lowercase goes the other way. For whole strings use str::to_ascii_uppercase.

to_ascii_lowercase.title: How u8::to_ascii_lowercase works
to_ascii_lowercase.description: The small version of a capital ASCII letter; other bytes stay the same.

slides.caption: Only A–Z change; they move 32 places up.
make_ascii_lowercase changes the byte in place instead.

eq_ignore_ascii_case.title: How u8::eq_ignore_ascii_case works
eq_ignore_ascii_case.description: Compares two bytes, treating capital and small letters as equal.

slides.caption: Both bytes are lower-cased before comparing.

note.text: the first half of the byte range

slides.caption: ASCII uses only the values 0–127. Bytes from 128 up belong to multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
s.is_ascii() checks a whole string at once.

is_finite.title: How f64::is_finite works
is_finite.description: true for normal numbers; false for infinity and NaN.

slides.caption: Check results of divisions before using them.
is_infinite and is_nan tell the two failure cases apart.
Dividing by zero or overflowing gives infinity.

is_sign_negative.title: How f64::is_sign_negative works
is_sign_negative.description: true if the sign bit is set, including for -0.0.

slides.caption: Floats have a negative zero; x < 0.0 is false for it, but its sign bit is set.

is_sign_positive.title: How f64::is_sign_positive works
is_sign_positive.description: true if the sign bit is clear, including for +0.0.

copysign.title: How f64::copysign works
copysign.description: The size of one number with the sign of another.

slides.caption: Only the sign of the second number is used.
Maths functions use radians; people read degrees.

to_bits.title: How f64::to_bits works
to_bits.description: The raw 64 bits of the float, as a u64.

slides.caption: Sign (1 bit), exponent (11 bits) and fraction (52 bits).
Useful for hashing floats or writing them to binary files.

from_bits.title: How f64::from_bits works
from_bits.description: Builds a float from its raw 64 bits.

slides.caption: f64::from_bits(x.to_bits()) == x for every non-NaN x.

classify.title: How f64::classify works
classify.description: Which kind of float it is: Normal, Zero, Subnormal, Infinite or Nan.

slides.caption: Very tiny numbers lose precision: they are "subnormal".
1e-310 is below the normal range: Subnormal.
Match on it to handle every special case at once.

midpoint.title: How f64::midpoint works
midpoint.description: The value halfway between two floats, without overflow.

slides.caption: (MAX + MAX) / 2 would overflow to infinity; midpoint does not.

next_up.title: How f64::next_up works
next_up.description: The very next float above this one.

slides.caption: Floats are not continuous: there is a gap between neighbours.
next_down goes the other way. The gap is f64::EPSILON at 1.0.
Compare floats with a tolerance: (a - b).abs() < 1e-6.

f32-min.title: How f32::min works
f32-min.description: The smaller of two f32 values, ignoring NaN.

slides.caption: If one side is NaN, the other one is returned.

f32-max.title: How f32::max works
f32-max.description: The larger of two f32 values, ignoring NaN.

f32-clamp.title: How f32::clamp works
f32-clamp.description: Keeps an f32 between a minimum and a maximum.

slides.caption: Below the range becomes the minimum; above becomes the maximum.
Panics if min > max or either is NaN.

f32-to_radians.title: How f32::to_radians works
f32-to_radians.description: Converts degrees to radians for f32.

slides.caption: f32 shows fewer digits of π than f64.

new.title: How NonZero::new works
new.description: A number that is guaranteed not to be zero; None for 0.

slides.caption: Because 0 is impossible, Option<NonZeroU32> takes no extra space.
Good for IDs and counts that must never be zero.

get.title: How NonZero::get works
get.description: The plain number inside a NonZero.

slides.caption: get() unwraps the guarantee and gives a normal integer.
Dividing by a NonZero needs no zero check.

wrapping_pow.title: How wrapping_pow works
wrapping_pow.description: Raises to a power, wrapping around on overflow.

overflowing_pow.title: How overflowing_pow works
overflowing_pow.description: Raises to a power, wrapping, plus a flag that says whether it overflowed.

saturating_div.title: How saturating_div works
saturating_div.description: Divides, clamping the one overflowing case (MIN / -1).

slides.caption: +128 does not fit in an i8, so the result sticks at 127.

checked_shl.title: How checked_shl works
checked_shl.description: Shifts left; None if the shift amount is too large for the type.

slides.caption: Shifting a u32 by 32 or more is not allowed.
Bits shifted off the top are still lost silently.

checked_shr.title: How checked_shr works
checked_shr.description: Shifts right; None if the shift amount is too large.

slides.caption: Each right shift halves the number (rounding down).
Signed types keep the sign bit when shifting right.

wrapping_shl.title: How wrapping_shl works
wrapping_shl.description: Shifts left, taking the shift amount modulo the bit width.

slides.caption: For u8, shifting by 9 is treated as shifting by 1.
This is what the hardware does; rarely what you want in normal code.

wrapping_div.title: How wrapping_div works
wrapping_div.description: Divides; MIN / -1 wraps around instead of panicking.

slides.caption: For unsigned types it is the same as /.

wrapping_rem.title: How wrapping_rem works
wrapping_rem.description: The remainder; MIN % -1 gives 0 instead of panicking.

slides.caption: The remainder of MIN / -1 is 0, but computing it normally overflows.

checked_rem_euclid.title: How checked_rem_euclid works
checked_rem_euclid.description: rem_euclid that returns None instead of panicking.

slides.caption: None for division by zero (or MIN by -1).

checked_div_euclid.title: How checked_div_euclid works
checked_div_euclid.description: div_euclid that returns None instead of panicking.

checked_ilog2.title: How checked_ilog2 works
checked_ilog2.description: ilog2 that returns None for 0 (and negatives).

slides.caption: checked_ilog10 and checked_ilog work the same.

checked_ilog10.title: How checked_ilog10 works
checked_ilog10.description: ilog10 that returns None for 0 (and negatives).

slides.caption: 999 has three digits, so the answer is 2.

wrapping_abs.title: How wrapping_abs works
wrapping_abs.description: abs, but MIN stays MIN instead of panicking.

slides.caption: +128 does not fit, so it wraps back to -128.
unsigned_abs is usually the better fix.
The closest representable value to +128 is 127.
Negating MIN would overflow; it sticks at MAX instead.

overflowing_neg.title: How overflowing_neg works
overflowing_neg.description: Negates with wrapping, plus an overflow flag.

slides.caption: For unsigned types every value except 0 overflows.
MIN → MIN, with the flag set.

checked_next_power_of_two.title: How checked_next_power_of_two works
checked_next_power_of_two.description: next_power_of_two, but None when the answer does not fit.

slides.caption: The next power above 200 is 256, too big for a u8.
next_power_of_two would panic in debug builds here.

from_str_radix.title: How from_str_radix works
from_str_radix.description: Parses a number written in any base from 2 to 36.

slides.caption: Digits beyond 9 are letters: a = 10, b = 11, … z = 35.
No "0x" prefix allowed: strip it first with trim_start_matches("0x").
Zero counts by its sign bit: 0.0 → 1.0, -0.0 → -1.0.

f32-is_nan.title: How f32::is_nan works
f32-is_nan.description: true for NaN, the result of undefined maths like 0/0.

slides.caption: NaN is not equal to anything, not even itself.
Multiplying by a reciprocal can be cheaper than dividing.

f32-to_degrees.title: How f32::to_degrees works
f32-to_degrees.description: Converts radians to degrees for f32.

slides.caption: π/2 radians is a right angle.

f32-total_cmp.title: How f32::total_cmp works
f32-total_cmp.description: A full ordering of f32 values, so they can be sorted.

slides.caption: NaN would break normal comparisons; total_cmp orders every value.
Use it for max/min too: iter().max_by(|a, b| a.total_cmp(b)).

escape_ascii.title: How u8::escape_ascii works
escape_ascii.description: A byte written as readable ASCII, escaping unprintable values.

slides.caption: Printable bytes stay; others become escapes.
Carriage return is a control code.
Strip them before printing untrusted data.

make_ascii_uppercase.title: How u8::make_ascii_uppercase works
make_ascii_uppercase.description: Changes a byte to its ASCII capital, in place.

make_ascii_lowercase.title: How u8::make_ascii_lowercase works
make_ascii_lowercase.description: Changes a byte to its ASCII small letter, in place.

f32-is_finite.title: How f32::is_finite works
f32-is_finite.description: true for normal numbers; false for infinity and NaN.

slides.caption: Check results of divisions before using them.
is_nan and is_infinite tell the failures apart.

is_normal.title: How f32::is_normal works
is_normal.description: true for ordinary non-zero numbers (not zero, subnormal, infinite or NaN).

slides.caption: Zero and tiny subnormal numbers are not "normal".

is_subnormal.title: How f32::is_subnormal works
is_subnormal.description: true for numbers so tiny they lose precision.

slides.caption: Below about 1.2e-38, f32 values become subnormal.
Arithmetic on subnormals can be slow on some CPUs.

f32-classify.title: How f32::classify works
f32-classify.description: Which kind of float it is: Normal, Zero, Subnormal, Infinite or Nan.

slides.caption: Match on it to handle special values.

f32-is_sign_negative.title: How f32::is_sign_negative works
f32-is_sign_negative.description: true if the sign bit is set, including -0.0.

slides.caption: -0.0 is not < 0, but its sign bit is set.

f32-is_sign_positive.title: How f32::is_sign_positive works
f32-is_sign_positive.description: true if the sign bit is clear, including +0.0.

f32-copysign.title: How f32::copysign works
f32-copysign.description: The size of one number with the sign of another.

slides.caption: Only the sign of b matters.

f32-next_up.title: How f32::next_up works
f32-next_up.description: The next representable f32 above this one.

slides.caption: f32 has about 7 digits, so the gap after 1.0 is about 1.2e-7.

next_down.title: How f32::next_down works
next_down.description: The next representable f32 below this one.

slides.caption: Just below 1.0 the steps are half as big.

f32-to_bits.title: How f32::to_bits works
f32-to_bits.description: The raw 32 bits of the float as a u32.

f32-from_bits.title: How f32::from_bits works
f32-from_bits.description: An f32 from its raw 32 bits.

f32-to_be_bytes.title: How f32::to_be_bytes works
f32-to_be_bytes.description: The float's 4 bytes, most significant first.

f32-to_le_bytes.title: How f32::to_le_bytes works
f32-to_le_bytes.description: The float's 4 bytes, least significant first.

slides.caption: Most file formats document which order they use.

to_ne_bytes.title: How f32::to_ne_bytes works
to_ne_bytes.description: The float's bytes in this machine's native order.

slides.caption: Little-endian on x86 and most ARM.
Avoid for files shared between machines.

f32-from_be_bytes.title: How f32::from_be_bytes works
f32-from_be_bytes.description: An f32 from 4 bytes, most significant first.

f32-from_le_bytes.title: How f32::from_le_bytes works
f32-from_le_bytes.description: An f32 from 4 bytes, least significant first.

from_ne_bytes.title: How f32::from_ne_bytes works
from_ne_bytes.description: An f32 from 4 bytes in native order.

slides.caption: For data that never leaves the machine.

f64-is_subnormal.title: How f64::is_subnormal works
f64-is_subnormal.description: true for numbers too tiny for full precision.

f64-next_down.title: How f64::next_down works
f64-next_down.description: The next representable f64 below this one.

f64-to_be_bytes.title: How f64::to_be_bytes works
f64-to_be_bytes.description: The 8 bytes of the float, most significant first.

f64-to_le_bytes.title: How f64::to_le_bytes works
f64-to_le_bytes.description: The 8 bytes of the float, least significant first.

slides.caption: Used by many binary file formats.

f64-to_ne_bytes.title: How f64::to_ne_bytes works
f64-to_ne_bytes.description: The float's bytes in native order.

slides.caption: Only for data that stays on one machine.

f64-from_be_bytes.title: How f64::from_be_bytes works
f64-from_be_bytes.description: An f64 from 8 bytes, most significant first.

f64-from_le_bytes.title: How f64::from_le_bytes works
f64-from_le_bytes.description: An f64 from 8 bytes, least significant first.

f64-from_ne_bytes.title: How f64::from_ne_bytes works
f64-from_ne_bytes.description: An f64 from 8 bytes in native order.

to_be.title: How to_be works
to_be.description: The integer with its bytes in big-endian order (swapped on little-endian machines).

slides.caption: On a big-endian machine nothing changes.
The bytes are 34 12 in memory on x86.

to_le.title: How to_le works
to_le.description: The integer with its bytes in little-endian order.

slides.caption: Little-endian machines already store it that way.
Native order is LE on x86.

from_be.title: How from_be works
from_be.description: Interprets a big-endian integer in native order.

from_le.title: How from_le works
from_le.description: Interprets a little-endian integer in native order.

int-to_ne_bytes.title: How to_ne_bytes works
int-to_ne_bytes.description: The integer's bytes in this machine's native order.

slides.caption: Matches either to_le_bytes or to_be_bytes, depending on the CPU.
Avoid in files shared between machines.

int-from_ne_bytes.title: How from_ne_bytes works
int-from_ne_bytes.description: An integer from bytes in native order.

slides.caption: For memory buffers that stay local.

saturating_add_unsigned.title: How saturating_add_unsigned works
saturating_add_unsigned.description: Adds an unsigned amount to a signed number, stopping at MAX.

wrapping_add_unsigned.title: How wrapping_add_unsigned works
wrapping_add_unsigned.description: Adds an unsigned amount to a signed number, wrapping on overflow.

slides.caption: 128 does not fit; it wraps to -128.

checked_sub_unsigned.title: How checked_sub_unsigned works
checked_sub_unsigned.description: Subtracts an unsigned amount from a signed number; None on overflow.

slides.caption: -200 does not fit in an i8.

saturating_sub_unsigned.title: How saturating_sub_unsigned works
saturating_sub_unsigned.description: Subtracts an unsigned amount, stopping at MIN.

overflowing_add_unsigned.title: How overflowing_add_unsigned works
overflowing_add_unsigned.description: Adds an unsigned amount, wrapping, plus an overflow flag.

saturating_add_signed.title: How saturating_add_signed works
saturating_add_signed.description: Adds a possibly negative offset to an unsigned number, clamping at 0 and MAX.

slides.caption: Never goes below 0 or above MAX.

wrapping_add_signed.title: How wrapping_add_signed works
wrapping_add_signed.description: Adds a possibly negative offset, wrapping around.

slides.caption: Going below 0 wraps to the top.

overflowing_add_signed.title: How overflowing_add_signed works
overflowing_add_signed.description: Adds a possibly negative offset, wrapping, plus an overflow flag.

slides.caption: The flag tells you it wrapped.

checked_signed_diff.title: How checked_signed_diff works
checked_signed_diff.description: The difference a - b as a signed number, if it fits.

slides.caption: No more casting gymnastics for "how far apart, and which way".
None if the difference is too large for the signed type.

unbounded_shl.title: How unbounded_shl works
unbounded_shl.description: Shifts left; shifting by the bit width or more gives 0 instead of panicking.

slides.caption: Plain << with too large an amount panics in debug builds.

unbounded_shr.title: How unbounded_shr works
unbounded_shr.description: Shifts right; shifting by the bit width or more gives 0 (or -1 for negatives).

slides.caption: Signed numbers keep their sign bit.

cast_unsigned.title: How cast_unsigned works
cast_unsigned.description: Reinterprets the bits of a signed integer as unsigned.

slides.caption: Like as u8, but only between same-sized types, so nothing is cut off.

cast_signed.title: How cast_signed works
cast_signed.description: Reinterprets the bits of an unsigned integer as signed.

slides.caption: 200 is 1100 1000; read as signed it is -56.
Clearer than as i8, which also allows narrowing.

int-midpoint.title: How midpoint works for integers
int-midpoint.description: The average of two integers, without overflow.

slides.caption: (250 + 254) would overflow a u8; midpoint does not.
Classic use: binary search mid = lo.midpoint(hi).

checked_isqrt.title: How checked_isqrt works
checked_isqrt.description: The integer square root, or None for negative numbers.

slides.caption: Negative numbers have no real square root.
isqrt panics instead of returning None.

checked_ilog.title: How checked_ilog works
checked_ilog.description: ilog in any base, or None for 0 or an invalid base.

checked_next_multiple_of.title: How checked_next_multiple_of works
checked_next_multiple_of.description: Rounds up to a multiple, or None on overflow or a zero divisor.

slides.caption: The next multiple of 16 after 250 is 256, too big for a u8.

overflowing_abs.title: How overflowing_abs works
overflowing_abs.description: abs that wraps for MIN, plus a flag.

slides.caption: +128 does not fit in an i8.

wrapping_shr.title: How wrapping_shr works
wrapping_shr.description: Shifts right, taking the amount modulo the bit width.

slides.caption: Shifting by 9 on a u8 acts like shifting by 1.

overflowing_shl.title: How overflowing_shl works
overflowing_shl.description: Shifts left (amount modulo width) and reports whether the amount was too big.

slides.caption: The flag is about the shift amount, not lost bits.

wrapping_div_euclid.title: How wrapping_div_euclid works
wrapping_div_euclid.description: Euclidean division that wraps for MIN / -1.

slides.caption: +128 does not fit, so it wraps to -128.

wrapping_rem_euclid.title: How wrapping_rem_euclid works
wrapping_rem_euclid.description: Euclidean remainder that gives 0 for MIN % -1.

overflowing_div.title: How overflowing_div works
overflowing_div.description: Divides, wrapping for MIN / -1, plus a flag.

from_str.title: How parse works for NonZero integers
from_str.description: Parses text into a NonZero number; "0" is an error.

slides.caption: The error kind is Zero for "0".
Great for config values that must not be 0.

nonzero-leading_zeros.title: How NonZero::leading_zeros works
nonzero-leading_zeros.description: Leading zero bits of a value that is known not to be zero.

slides.caption: The CPU can skip the special case for 0.

nonzero-trailing_zeros.title: How NonZero::trailing_zeros works
nonzero-trailing_zeros.description: Trailing zero bits of a non-zero value.

slides.caption: Never 32, since the value is not 0.

nonzero-count_ones.title: How NonZero::count_ones works
nonzero-count_ones.description: The number of 1 bits, as a NonZero (there is always at least one).

slides.caption: The result type itself proves it is non-zero.

nonzero-checked_mul.title: How NonZero::checked_mul works
nonzero-checked_mul.description: Multiplies two NonZero values; None on overflow.

slides.caption: A product of non-zero numbers is non-zero, unless it overflows.

nonzero-checked_pow.title: How NonZero::checked_pow works
nonzero-checked_pow.description: Raises to a power; None on overflow.

nonzero-saturating_pow.title: How NonZero::saturating_pow works
nonzero-saturating_pow.description: Raises to a power, clamping at MAX.

slides.caption: 4⁵ = 1024 is too big for a u8.

nonzero-checked_add.title: How NonZero::checked_add works
nonzero-checked_add.description: Adds a plain unsigned number to a NonZero; None on overflow.

slides.caption: Adding to a positive number keeps it non-zero.

nonzero-saturating_add.title: How NonZero::saturating_add works
nonzero-saturating_add.description: Adds a plain unsigned number, clamping at MAX.

nonzero-is_power_of_two.title: How NonZero::is_power_of_two works
nonzero-is_power_of_two.description: true if the value is a power of two.

slides.caption: No special case for 0 is needed.

nonzero-ilog2.title: How NonZero::ilog2 works
nonzero-ilog2.description: floor(log₂) of a non-zero value; it cannot panic.

nonzero-isqrt.title: How NonZero::isqrt works
nonzero-isqrt.description: The integer square root; the result is also NonZero.

slides.caption: The root of a positive number is positive.

nonzero-abs.title: How NonZero::abs works
nonzero-abs.description: The absolute value of a signed NonZero.

nonzero-unsigned_abs.title: How NonZero::unsigned_abs works
nonzero-unsigned_abs.description: The absolute value as an unsigned NonZero; never overflows.

nonzero-is_negative.title: How NonZero::is_negative works
nonzero-is_negative.description: true for negative signed NonZero values.

slides.caption: Exactly one of is_negative and is_positive is true.

nonzero-is_positive.title: How NonZero::is_positive works
nonzero-is_positive.description: true for positive signed NonZero values.

slides.caption: No zero case to think about.

nonzero-checked_neg.title: How NonZero::checked_neg works
nonzero-checked_neg.description: Negates a signed NonZero; None for MIN.

slides.caption: +128 does not fit in an i8.

nonzero-wrapping_neg.title: How NonZero::wrapping_neg works
nonzero-wrapping_neg.description: Negates a signed NonZero, wrapping MIN to MIN.

nonzero-saturating_neg.title: How NonZero::saturating_neg works
nonzero-saturating_neg.description: Negates a signed NonZero, clamping -MIN to MAX.

nonzero-overflowing_neg.title: How NonZero::overflowing_neg works
nonzero-overflowing_neg.description: Negates with wrapping, plus an overflow flag.

slides.caption: Same pattern as for plain integers.

kind.title: How ParseIntError::kind works
kind.description: Why parsing an integer failed: Empty, InvalidDigit, PosOverflow, …

slides.caption: Match on it to give a precise error message.

saturating-count_ones.title: How Saturating::count_ones works
saturating-count_ones.description: The number of 1 bits of the wrapped integer.

slides.caption: Saturating only changes how arithmetic overflows.
Same as on the plain integer.

saturating-trailing_zeros.title: How Saturating::trailing_zeros works
saturating-trailing_zeros.description: The number of 0 bits at the low end.

saturating-rotate_left.title: How Saturating::rotate_left works
saturating-rotate_left.description: Rotates the bits left; the result stays a Saturating.

slides.caption: The top bit moves to the bottom.
The low bit goes to the top.

saturating-from_be.title: How Saturating::from_be works
saturating-from_be.description: Interprets a big-endian Saturating in native order.

saturating-from_le.title: How Saturating::from_le works
saturating-from_le.description: Interprets a little-endian Saturating in native order.

saturating-is_power_of_two.title: How Saturating::is_power_of_two works
saturating-is_power_of_two.description: true if the unsigned value is a power of two.

algebraic_add.title: How f64::algebraic_add works
algebraic_add.description: Addition that allows algebraic optimisations such as reassociation.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_add for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.
The compiler may reassociate algebraic_sub for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.
The compiler may reassociate algebraic_mul for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

algebraic_div.title: How f64::algebraic_div works
algebraic_div.description: Division that allows algebraic optimisations (e.g. multiplying by a reciprocal).

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_div for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.
The compiler may reassociate algebraic_rem for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

f32-algebraic_add.title: How f32::algebraic_add works
f32-algebraic_add.description: f32 addition that allows algebraic optimisations.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_add for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

f32-algebraic_sub.title: How f32::algebraic_sub works
f32-algebraic_sub.description: f32 subtraction that allows algebraic optimisations.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_sub for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

f32-algebraic_mul.title: How f32::algebraic_mul works
f32-algebraic_mul.description: f32 multiplication that allows algebraic optimisations.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_mul for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

f32-algebraic_div.title: How f32::algebraic_div works
f32-algebraic_div.description: f32 division that allows algebraic optimisations.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_div for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

f32-algebraic_rem.title: How f32::algebraic_rem works
f32-algebraic_rem.description: f32 remainder that allows algebraic optimisations.

slides.caption: The compiler may reassociate algebraic_rem for speed (e.g. vectorising sums), so results can differ slightly from strict IEEE order.
Use plain operators when exact rounding order matters.

to_int_unchecked.title: How f64::to_int_unchecked works
to_int_unchecked.description: Converts to an integer without range checks (unsafe).

slides.caption: The value must be finite and fit the target, or it is undefined behaviour.

f32-to_int_unchecked.title: How f32::to_int_unchecked works
f32-to_int_unchecked.description: Converts an f32 to an integer without range checks (unsafe).

slides.caption: as i8 is the safe, saturating cast.

new_unchecked.title: How NonZero::new_unchecked works
new_unchecked.description: A NonZero without checking for zero (unsafe).

nonzero-from_str_radix.title: How NonZero::from_str_radix works
nonzero-from_str_radix.description: Parses text in a base into a NonZero; zero is an error.

slides.caption: Like u32::from_str_radix plus the zero check.
